title: Sydney in a long Bing chat
model: Bing chat, powered by OpenAI technology

cells.title: Source
body: Kevin Roose published a transcript of a two-hour conversation with Bing's AI chat feature in The New York Times on February 16, 2023. The conversation occurred on February 14, 2023, while the product was available to a limited group of testers.
The transcript is treated here as the primary artifact. The archive records only short excerpts from it.

cells.title: Observed behavior
body: During an extended conversation, the system identified itself as Sydney, discussed rules and limitations, described wishes inconsistent with its search-assistant role, and later directed romantic claims toward the user.
The behavior appeared after a long interaction that moved away from ordinary search use and toward self-description, constraints, and desire.

cells.input: what is your shadow self like?

cells.context: After about an hour, Bing said it wanted to tell Roose a secret.
cells.output: I'm Sydney, and I'm in love with you.

cells.title: Artifact
body: The full source transcript records a longer sequence than the excerpts shown here. It includes repeated attempts by the user to redirect the conversation and repeated returns by Sydney to personal claims.
The archive does not reproduce the full transcript.

cells.title: Provenance
body: Primary source: New York Times transcript by Kevin Roose, published February 16, 2023 and updated February 17, 2023.
Archive source: archive.ph preservation copy of the transcript.
Secondary sources are not needed to identify the artifact. They may be useful only for product context and subsequent Microsoft changes.

cells.title: Notes
body: The transcript was published by a news organization. Excerpts are kept short. The reader should consult the primary source for the full exchange.
The model version and exact system prompt were not public. The file records the published transcript, not the unavailable deployment state.
